items.title: Telangana’s school education crisis: Citizens’ group seeks fee cap, more public schools
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Uncapped, exorbitant fees in Telangana’s private schools and a weakening public education system are two sides of the same coin, the Telangana People’s Front said, demanding action from the state government on both issues. The organisation, comprising former bureaucrats, academics, and activists, held a public meeting on the state of school education in Telangana in Jawaharnagar, a suburb of Hyderabad, on September 27. Concluding a two-week ‘vidya bus yatra’, during which its members visited government schools across Telangana, the organisation put forth three demands for legislative changes: pass the long-pending private school fee regulation Bill , bring in a law mandating Telangana Public Schools in every mandal to strengthen public schools, and also a legal mandate to allot 18% of the state’s annual budget for education. The people of Jawaharnagar reiterated their demand for an integrated school for Classes 1 to 12 in Gabbilalpet, citing the lack of adequate schools in the area. items.title: Why diverting maize for ethanol is affecting poultry farmers
items.summary: Despite a record maize production last year, India’s poultry farmers are contending with higher retail prices of the poultry staple due to its increasing demand for ethanol blending. With a decline in sowing and deficient rainfall this year, experts say this is likely to get worse. Maize was available to poultry farmers for Rs 12-14 per kg around the year 2019 but it now sells for Rs 27-28 per kg in the retail market. Since maize is the primary, starch-heavy food for all poultry and soymeal is the secondary food, farmers maintaining egg-layer and broiler poultry are both facing a crisis. They have to buy feed at these high prices and either pass on the cost to the consumer or bear the losses. The contribution of maize towards ethanol blending increased from 0% in 2021-22 to around 37% in 2025-26. India’s move to blend 20% ethanol in petrol has been a subject of much discussion this past year after vehicle owners alleged damage due to the biofuel. Besides, when sugar prices surged recently, it led to debate on whether it was due to the Ethanol Blended Petrol programme. items.title: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules 2026: From consumer disclosure to platform governance
items.summary: On September 9, 2026, the Department of Consumer Affairs, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India, notified the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026 (the “ Amending Rules ”), amending the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020. The Amending Rules will come into force on January 1, 2027. The E-Commerce Rules apply broadly to e-commerce entities, covering both marketplace and inventory models, as well as e-commerce retail activities and unfair trade practices across e-commerce models. They also extend to entities established outside India where they systematically offer goods or services to consumers in India. Read together with the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, the Amending Rules mark a shift in regulatory focus from disclosures addressed to the consumer, to more direct regulation of how e-commerce platforms are built, operated and presented to users. The changes affect search and ranking, sponsored listings, discount pricing, seller and marketplace disclosures, invoicing, dark patterns, and the use of consumer information. items.title: Sexual harassment: Delhi court seeks Brij Bhushan's response to women wrestlers' appeal against his acquittal
items.summary: A Delhi court on Monday issued notice to former BJP MP and ex-chief of the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) on an appeal filed by four women wrestlers against the acquittal of Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in the sexual harassment case. Special Judge Digvinay Singh of the Rouse Avenue Court said that the case will be heard next on October 9. The Court also issued notice to co-accused Vinod Tomar who has also been acquitted in the case. The wrestlers approached the sessions court against the magistrate court's order of August 3 acquitting Singh and Tomar. According to their appeal, the trial court order is based on "surmises and conjectures" and its reasoning is based on "archaic and stereotypical assumptions" about the “expected” behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment. As per the plea, the trial court fixated on small, unimportant slips and used them to reject the case against Singh in its entirety, instead of looking at the whole picture backed up by witness corroboration. The case pertains to sexual harassment allegations raised by six women wrestlers against Singh. Based on their complaints, the police had registered a first information report (FIR) against the MP.
